topPRs.title: op-acceptance-tests: use time travel for L1 finality in slow memory-all tests
topPRs.author: mds1
topPRs.body:
- `TestFinalizedL2DoesNotRegressAcrossActivation`: 381s -> 291s.
- `TestZK_HonestChallenger_ChildOfInvalidParent_ChallengerWins`: 346s -> 117s.
- `TestSupernodeInterop_SafeHeadProgression`: 164s -> 55-60s.
- memory-all slowest node: 398-422s -> 339-353s. Job: 470-515s -> 418-459s. Same 884 tests per job, all green ([139145](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/139145), [139136](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/139136), [139138](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/139138)).
- These tests spent most of their time waiting for FakePoS L1 finality in real time (20 blocks of 6s). Each now jumps the L1 clock with the existing time-travel support, so FakePoS builds those blocks in seconds, and then waits for the same finality condition as before. `SafeHeadProgression` already jumped, but read the head after the jump, so it still waited the full 20 blocks.

Why it's safe:
- No assertion is removed or loosened. The challenger's finalized-parent gate, the challenge windows and the 30 minute credit delay are unchanged. Only L1 block production is faster.
- Activation test: the 240s activation delay only existed to fit the first finality wait. It is now 150s, which keeps most of the old setup margin. New checks fail the test loudly, instead of passing vacuously, if setup is ever slow enough for LocalSafe to cross activation before the baseline is taken.
- ZK test: the two jumps use about 5 of the roughly 30 minutes left in the child challenge windows. A planted regression (the challenger not challenging a child of an invalid parent) still fails the test.
- Each jump stays under FakePoS's 5 minute skip, so it builds the full ~25 blocks instead of a single one.

topPRs.title: kona-client: make the FPVM binary dependencies optional
topPRs.author: yoshidan
topPRs.body:
`kona-client`'s library — `fpvm_evm`, `interop`, `single` — never references `kona_std_fpvm`; only the two binary sources do. Declaring the dependency unconditionally means a consumer that wants the library alone cannot build for a `no_std` target, because `kona-std-fpvm` reads the preimage oracle over file descriptors and carries no `#![no_std]`. We hit this building an SGX enclave around `FpvmOpEvmFactory`.

This does not make `kona-client` a `no_std` crate; it only stops the library from dragging in a dependency that none of it uses.

No effect on existing users: `default` still enables `client-tracing`, and now `fpvm` explicitly, so both binaries build as before. Only a consumer that opts out with `default-features = false` sees a difference. `client-tracing` keeps `fpvm` in its list because `kona-std-fpvm/tracing` alone would leave `kona-std-fpvm-proc` disabled and the binaries unbuildable.

`kona-client` joins `no_std_packages` so `just check-no-std` keeps this from regressing.

Closes #23993

Checks run locally: `just check-no-std` (21 packages, including the new entry), `just fmt-check`, `cargo build -p kona-client` (both binaries produced), `cargo test -p kona-client`. I did not run the full `just lint`; its `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features` does not finish in reasonable time on my machine. Package-scoped clippy reports a pre-existing `const fn` lint in `kona-derive` that comes from building it without its `metrics` feature, which the workspace-wide `--all-features` run does not do.

No review agent's trigger matches this diff: it changes no Rust source, and `rust/justfile` is outside `ci-config-reviewer`'s `.circleci/` and `.github/workflows/` scope.
